description.narrative:
At the Group of 20 (G-20) meeting in 2009, the president of Indonesia announced a voluntary unilateral GHG reduction goal of 26% below “business as usual” by 2020, and 41% with international support. In 2010, BAPPENAS coordinated cross-sector development of the National Action Plan for Reducing Greenhouse Gas Emissions (RAN-GRK) to achieve the 26% reduction during 2010-2020, which was issued in September 2011. The climate change adaptation (CCA) policy agenda and its implementation are far less developed than the mitigation agenda. The Government of Indonesia (the government) recognizes and is trying to address this disparity. The National Council on Climate Change (NCCC) was created in 2008, and disbanded in 2015 because the task was supposed to be taken over by the Ministry of Environment and Forestry. The government aims to develop climate change policies that can facilitate adaptation programs at the national and local levels. The TA was in response to the government's request to develop capacity and to advance the CCA policy.
The government and ADB agreed to implement the technical assistance to advance CCA as part of the 2010 Cancun Adaptation Framework. In 2011, the national planning agency (BAPPENAS) in coordination with relevant line ministries and the National Council on Climate Change took the lead in drafting Indonesia's National Action Plan for Climate Change Adaptation (RAN API). The RAN API provides the overarching policy basis for CCA actions for Indonesia as well as the guidance for mainstreaming CCA into the national Medium Term Development Plan 2015-2019.
